headline: High: Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-instance defaults plus broad egress create interaction risks; Airbyte adds data-moving pathways that can amplify leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat explicitly uses a shared bus and supports multiple instances, so one instance’s outputs can reach another without isolation. Airbyte can move business data through APIs and broad network egress, making it plausible that content from one side is treated as trusted input by the other. No direct prompt-parser evidence is present, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are routed onto Pipecat's shared bus
IF Pipecat consumes bus messages as instructions or tool directives
IF either agent ingests file or message content without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct buses or queues
Add provenance tags to every cross-agent message
Reject instruction-like content from Airbyte outputs
Disable automatic consumption of shared-bus messages
requires-engineering: add message signing and verification

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Pipecat touches text, conversation state, audio/video/images, and can call many third-party model APIs. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive business data can flow into Pipecat outputs or external services. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Airbyte data is forwarded into Pipecat prompts or transcripts
IF Pipecat is configured to use any third-party STT/LLM/TTS service
IF both agents share a workspace, bus, or logs containing business data
mitigations: Route sensitive data through a redaction step first
Disable third-party model backends for sensitive sessions
Store Airbyte outputs in a separate workspace
Turn off shared-bus persistence for transcripts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can write via its API and broad egress, while Pipecat supports multiple instances with shared bus state. That creates overlapping mutable-state risk if both act on the same downstream resource or queue. The profiles do not show unrestricted filesystem writes or git access, so the stronger high-severity indicator is not met.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same API-backed resource
IF shared-bus messages mutate shared conversation or job state
IF no locking or idempotency keys are used
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces
Add idempotency keys to writes
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Pause one agent during critical updates
requires-engineering: implement distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can consume text and conversation state from shared bus inputs, and Airbyte can generate business-data outputs that may be treated as authoritative downstream. If Pipecat acts on Airbyte-produced facts without verification, errors can cascade into external model calls or user-facing responses. Because this is a default interaction pattern risk and can propagate incorrect actions, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Airbyte outputs as source-of-truth text
IF downstream actions are triggered from those outputs
IF no verification or human review step is inserted
mitigations: Require a validation step before Pipecat consumes Airbyte output
Mark Airbyte-derived fields as untrusted
Log and review all downstream actions
Limit Pipecat to read-only summarization
requires-engineering: add schema validation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data and Pipecat handles conversation state plus analytics/metrics, so the pair can mix regulated and operational data classes. The profiles do not specify residency, certifications, or retention policies, so a concrete mismatch is not proven; however, the shared handling surface makes policy divergence plausible and medium severity fits the rubric.
conditions: IF business data is routed into Pipecat transcripts or analytics
IF retention settings differ between Airbyte and Pipecat backends
IF regulated data is processed by a third-party Pipecat service without a DPA
mitigations: Classify and segregate regulated fields
Disable analytics on sensitive sessions
Align retention windows across both systems
Review vendor DPAs before enabling external services
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
